newsitem.title: USA: Florida ruling due shortly on Liggett documents.
newsitem.headline: Florida ruling due shortly on Liggett documents.

text.p: A court-appointed attorney reviewing Liggett Group papers sought by anti-tobacco lawyers said on Tuesday he would rule shortly on release of some of the documents.
William Rutter, appointed by the trial judge in the state of Florida's Medicaid lawsuit against tobacco companies, on Monday authorized the release of seven Liggett papers.

One of the documents was a lawyer's memorandum to Liggett, a unit of Brooke Group Ltd, advising the cigarette maker that a proposed advertising campaign for its Lark brand would invite cancer lawsuits.

Liggett on March 20 agreed to hand over to anti-tobacco lawyers five boxes of industry papers as part of a settlement with state attorneys general suing tobacco companies for some $30 billion spent treating sick smokers.
So far, the Liggett papers have been largely distributed only to judges considering tobacco company claims that many of the documents are legally protected from outsiders.
Rutter told Reuters after a second day of hearings in the Florida state Medicaid case that he would write a recommendation possibly as early as Thursday.
His decision would then be considered on Monday by the trial judge at a hearing in Palm Beach County Court.
